stages.title: Repository Initialization
stages.concept: Initializing a new Git repository using git init
learningObjectives: Create a new Git repository in a directory using git init
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Initializing a Git Repository

To turn any local directory into a Git repository, use the `git init` command. This creates a hidden `.git` directory containing all tracking metadata and object storage for your project.

```bash
git init
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Genesis Repository

Write a shell command to initialize a new Git repository in the current directory.
stages.starterCode: # Write the command to initialize a git repository

stages.title: Staging Changes
stages.concept: Adding files to the staging area using git add
prerequisites: Initializing a new Git repository using git init
learningObjectives: Stage files for commit using git add <filename>
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Staging Files in Git

Before recording a snapshot in Git, modified or newly created files must be added to the staging area (also known as the index) using `git add`.

```bash
git add index.html
git add .
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Staging Ground

Write a command to stage all modified and untracked files in the current working directory.

examples.explanation: Stages all files with git add .

stages.starterCode: # Write command to stage all files

stages.title: Committing Changes
stages.concept: Recording staged snapshots using git commit
prerequisites: Adding files to the staging area using git add
learningObjectives: Create a commit with a descriptive message using git commit -m
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Committing Changes

Save staged changes permanently into the repository history with an inline commit message using `git commit -m "message"`.

```bash
git commit -m "Initial commit"
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## First Record

Write a command to commit staged changes with the message `"Initial commit"`.

stages.title: Checking Status
stages.concept: Inspecting working tree status using git status
prerequisites: Recording staged snapshots using git commit
learningObjectives: Check staged, untracked, and modified file states with git status
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Checking Repository Status

The `git status` command displays the state of the working directory and the staging area. It shows which changes have been staged, which haven't, and which files aren't being tracked by Git.

```bash
git status
```
stages.problemStatementMd:

stages.title: Commit Log & History
stages.concept: Viewing commit history with git log
prerequisites: Inspecting working tree status using git status
learningObjectives: View historical commit history using git log
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Viewing Commit History

The `git log` command shows committed snapshots. Adding `--oneline` formats each commit into a single condensed line showing the short hash and commit message.

```bash
git log --oneline
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Chronicles of Code

Write a command to view compact, one-line commit history.

stages.title: Branch Creation
stages.concept: Creating feature branches with git branch
prerequisites: Viewing commit history with git log
learningObjectives: Create new branches using git branch <name>
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Creating Branches

Branches allow isolating development work without affecting the primary production branch. Use `git branch <branch-name>` to create a new branch pointer at your current HEAD.

```bash
git branch feature-login
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Parallel Timeline

Write a command to create a new branch named `feature`.

stages.title: Switching Branches
stages.concept: Switching branches using git checkout or git switch
prerequisites: Creating new branches using git branch <name>
learningObjectives: Switch working branches using git switch <name>
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Switching Branches

To move your HEAD pointer and working files to another branch, use `git checkout <branch-name>` or the modern `git switch <branch-name>` command.

```bash
git checkout feature
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Dimensional Shift

Write a command to switch to an existing branch named `feature`.

examples.explanation: Switches working directory to feature branch.

stages.starterCode: # Write command to switch to branch 'feature'

stages.title: Merging Branches
stages.concept: Merging branch histories using git merge
prerequisites: Switching working branches using git switch <name>
learningObjectives: Merge target branch changes into current branch using git merge
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Merging Branches

To integrate changes from another branch into your active working branch, run `git merge <target-branch>`:

```bash
git checkout main
git merge feature
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Convergence

Write the command to merge the `feature` branch into your currently checked out branch.

stages.title: Remote Repositories
stages.concept: Managing remote links with git remote add
prerequisites: Recording staged snapshots using git commit
learningObjectives: Add a remote repository shortcut using git remote add
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Adding Remote Repositories

To connect your local repository to a remote server (like GitHub or GitLab), use `git remote add <name> <url>` to create a named alias for the remote repository URL.

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git
```
stages.problemStatementMd:

stages.title: Pushing Changes
stages.concept: Uploading local commits to remote with git push
prerequisites: Add a remote repository shortcut using git remote add
learningObjectives: Push local branch commits to remote repository using git push
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Pushing to Remote Repositories

Upload local branch commits to your remote repository using `git push <remote-name> <branch-name>`. This synchronizes your local history with the shared remote server.

```bash
git push origin main
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Orbital Upload

Write a command to push the local `main` branch to the remote repository named `origin`.
